title: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral

topics.title: Litmus as an indicator: acidic, basic and neutral substances

concepts.learning_objective: Describe litmus as a natural acid-base indicator obtained from lichens and state its colour changes.
Classify common substances as acidic, basic or neutral from their effect on blue and red litmus paper.

topics.title: Taste, touch and acids in everyday substances

concepts.learning_objective: Name the common acids present in edible substances such as lemon, tamarind, amla, curd and vinegar.
Relate the sour taste of acids and the slippery feel and bitter taste of bases, recognising the limits of taste as a test.

topics.title: Red rose and other natural indicators

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how red rose extract changes colour in acidic and basic solutions.
Identify other natural indicators such as beetroot, purple cabbage, jamun, red hibiscus and hydrangea flowers.
Use turmeric paper to detect basic substances and explain why it cannot tell acidic from neutral substances.
Explain what olfactory indicators are, using onion-soaked strips as an example.

topics.title: Neutralisation: when acids mix with bases

concepts.learning_objective: State that an acid and a base neutralise each other to form salt and water with the release of heat.
Interpret indicator colour changes that show an acidic or basic solution being neutralised.
Explain why moist baking soda relieves the sting of a red ant bite.
Choose suitable treatments for acidic, basic and neutral soils with poor plant growth.
Explain how acidic factory waste can be neutralised before it is released into water bodies.
